<timestamp>Thursday, Aug 20, 2026, 9:42 PM (UTC-7)</timestamp>
<user_query>
Is there anything to improve in AGENTS.md?
</user_query>
I'll read `AGENTS.md` against the rest of the repo and look for gaps, duplication, or stale guidance.

Yes. The file is doing the right job — trust constraints at the root, scoped rules in nested `AGENTS.md` files — but a few places are stale or hard for an agent to use.

**Fix first: `packages/sidecar-core/` is gone.** The opening still says to put platform-independent behavior there. That package does not exist; logic lives in the named packages under `packages/` (`session`, `observation`, `surface`, and so on). The later “Repository shape” section already says this. `packages/surface/AGENTS.md` has the same leftover: generated files go to `packages/surface/src/generated/`, not `packages/sidecar-core/src/`. An agent following the first paragraph will invent the wrong import path.

**Keep the trust prose; make it jumpable.** Those long bullets are the product, not filler. Do not compress them into slogans. What would help is headings inside that list (Superset, Codex CLI, hooks, session writes, analytics, tracker, Google calendar, EventKit, ducking, mute, capture, updater). EventKit is currently a tail on the Google calendar bullet, so it is easy to miss.

**Tighten the index, not the law.** The “Where the rest of the guidance lives” table is the right split. Two small gaps:

- `docs/WORKFLOW.md` and `docs/DESIGN.md` are binding and required by repository checks, but the table does not name them. Design only appears once you are already in the renderer file.
- `packages/providers/AGENTS.md` still owns the `PRIVACY.md` analytics sentence. That now belongs in `packages/analytics/AGENTS.md`, which already says it.

**Twin `CLAUDE.md` files have no identity check.** Repository checks only require both files to exist. They look identical today; nothing fails if they drift. A `cmp` (or generating one from the other) would match how generated brand/surface files are treated.

I would not add nested guides for every package. Most of them inherit the root constraints, and more files would be more drift. A main-process `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md` is the only extra that might earn its keep (native helpers, IPC, updater), and only if that code keeps growing.

I would not rewrite the trust constraints for “readability.” The cost of a shorter file is an agent inventing a write path the long sentences currently forbid.

The one change I would make without debate is replacing `packages/sidecar-core/` in the root opener and in `packages/surface/AGENTS.md`. Want me to do that?
